statement: Write Q_i = (queens[i][0], queens[i][1]) and K = (king[0], king[1]). The function returns a result r, and the entries of r are exactly the coordinates Q_i, for 0 <= i < len(queens), such that Q_i can directly attack K. Specifically, Q_i can directly attack K iff Q_i != K, Q_i is aligned with K (Q_i[0] = K[0], or Q_i[1] = K[1], or |Q_i[0]-K[0]| = |Q_i[1]-K[1]|), and no Q_j with 0 <= j < len(queens) and j != i lies strictly between Q_i and K on the line segment joining them. Thus every attacking Q_i occurs in r exactly once, no other coordinate occurs in r, every entry of r has length 2, and the order of entries of r is arbitrary.
preconditions: len(queens) >= 1 and len(queens) < 64; len(king) = 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(queens), len(queens[i]) = 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(queens), 0 <= queens[i][0] < 8 and 0 <= queens[i][1] < 8; 0 <= king[0] < 8 and 0 <= king[1] < 8; the positions (queens[i][0], queens[i][1]) for 0 <= i < len(queens) are pairwise distinct, and none of them equals (king[0], king[1]).
